items.raw_claim: Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking are now available through Vercel AI Gateway's realtime WebSocket API.
items.summary: Google's Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking are now callable through Vercel AI Gateway's realtime API over WebSocket, using short-lived tokens and the AI SDK model adapter. The base model supports real-time audio, visual grounding, automatic switching across 97 languages and background tool calls mid-conversation; Extended Thinking adds reasoning that runs in parallel with speech. Gateway adds unified usage and cost tracking plus retries and failover across providers. For voice-agent work this is a credible second source for realtime speech-to-speech — worth a latency and cost spike before deepening a single-vendor dependency.
items.title: Gemini 3.8 Live models now available on Vercel AI Gateway
items.uncertainty: Latency, per-minute pricing and real-world interruption quality versus incumbent realtime providers are not stated in the changelog.
items.verdict_reason: Concrete platform availability change that directly affects a near-term voice-agent architecture decision.
items.worth_mentioning_reason: Adds a concrete second option for realtime voice agents behind an abstraction layer that already handles failover and cost tracking.

items.raw_claim: A free, working browser-based client for Google's new Gemini 3.8 Live speech-to-speech models is publicly available, with interrupt support and transcript export.
items.summary: Simon Willison shipped a small web UI for Google's newly released Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking speech-to-speech models, generated by pointing a coding model at the documentation. It supports model and voice-preset selection, an optional system prompt, a downloadable live transcript, and interrupting the model mid-sentence. It is the fastest available way to actually hear these models rather than read their spec sheet. Clone it instead of building a realtime test harness from scratch.
items.title: Gemini Live audio: a working browser client for the new speech-to-speech models
items.uncertainty: It is a demo harness, not production code — no error handling, reconnection or cost guardrails should be assumed.
items.verdict_reason: Reproducible, immediately usable artifact that shortens evaluation of a model family relevant to current work.
items.worth_mentioning_reason: Saves a day of realtime WebSocket plumbing for anyone evaluating speech-to-speech models this week.

items.raw_claim: Apple has published an approach called Reference Image for verifying that a photograph came from a genuine camera capture.
items.summary: Apple's security blog describes Reference Image, an approach for attesting that a photograph originated from a real camera capture rather than a generative model. If this lands as a platform primitive it changes the economics of any product that treats user-submitted photos as evidence, since authenticity stops being something each app has to solve alone. Anyone designing a homegrown image-attestation scheme should read this first. The item arrived without body text, so the post itself is the source of record.
items.title: Apple Reference Image: a new approach for verified photography
items.uncertainty: The fetched item had no body content, so availability, developer API surface and timeline are unconfirmed from this source.
items.verdict_reason: Credible first-party security publication on a problem that directly affects verification-oriented product work.
items.worth_mentioning_reason: Photo authenticity is an unsolved trust problem for any product accepting submitted images as evidence; a platform-level answer changes the build-versus-wait calculus.

items.raw_claim: Volunteer hosting collective Autistici/Inventati is shutting down after losing banking access, affecting roughly 20,000 mail accounts and 1,500 websites.
items.summary: Autistici/Inventati, a long-running volunteer-run hosting collective, is shutting down after losing financial access rather than for any technical reason; the announcement cites roughly 20,000 mail accounts, 20,000 blogs, 5,000 mailing lists and 1,500 websites affected. The operational lesson, independent of the politics around the case, is that payment-rail access is a single point of failure for small infrastructure in the same way a sole cloud provider is. Worth a few minutes thinking about what happens to your own project if a processor drops you.

items.raw_claim: Vercel's Is Agentic audit now presents its checks through four site-type views (content, business, app, commerce) selectable via a meta tag, without changing scores.

Scores stay comparable across views and a meta tag sets the default. Mildly useful if you care how an agent reads your site, but it reorders existing checks rather than adding capability.
